name: KPMG
summary: KPMG's interviews usually combine an assessment, technical questions for the practice you've applied to (audit, tax, advisory or consulting) and a conversation about fit and behaviour. KPMG in India publishes an indicative process: an online assessment, a group discussion, a case study round, then interviews with a recruiter and a technical panel. Elsewhere the steps vary by country and role.
rounds: Online assessment: comprehension, reasoning and psychometric questions (quantitative or data questions for some practices)
Case study round, written or as a discussion
Interview with a recruiter on fit and behaviour
Technical panel interview, sometimes with two or three interviewers
looks_for: Integrity: we do what is right
Excellence: we never stop learning and improving
Courage: we think and act boldly
Together: we respect each other and draw strength from our differences
For Better: we do what matters

questions.text: Tell me about yourself and why you're interested in professional services.
covers: Your studies or current role in two or three lines
One achievement that shows the skills this practice needs
Why advisory, audit or tax work appeals to you

questions.text: Tell me about a time you did the right thing when it would have been easier not to.
covers: The easier path and why it was tempting
What you did instead and who you involved
The result and what it says about how you work

questions.text: Tell me about a time you taught yourself something difficult so you could do better work.
covers: What you needed to learn and why
How you went about it, with specific resources or practice
How your work improved because of it

questions.text: Describe a time you suggested a bold idea. How did people react, and what happened?
covers: The idea and why it was a risk
How you made the case and handled doubts
The outcome, even if it didn't go your way, and what you learnt

questions.text: Tell me about a time you worked closely with someone very different from you to get a result.
covers: How you differed: background, working style or views
What you did to understand them and use their strengths
What you achieved together

questions.text: What is materiality in an audit, and how does it change what an auditor tests?
covers: The size of error that could change a reader's decision
How it's set, often from a benchmark such as profit or revenue, with judgement
How it guides sample sizes and where the audit team spends effort

questions.text: A client's inventory records don't match the warehouse count. How would you investigate?
covers: Checking the count itself first: timing, goods in transit, items held for others
Tracing differences to records: receipts, dispatches, returns, write-offs
The likely causes, the control that failed, and what you'd recommend

questions.text: Explain transfer pricing in simple terms, and why tax authorities care about it.
covers: The prices one part of a group charges another, often across countries
The arm's length idea: prices as if the two were unrelated
Why it matters: where profit is taxed, and the risk of disputes

questions.text: How would you assess whether a mid-sized company is ready to move to a new ERP system?
covers: Its reasons and goals, and what systems and processes it has today
Readiness: clean data, people's time and skills, budget and leadership support
Main risks and a phased plan with clear checkpoints

questions.text: A bank wants fewer false alarms from its anti-money-laundering checks without missing real cases. How would you approach it?
covers: Understanding the current rules, alert volumes and what share turn out to be real
Tuning thresholds, adding customer context, or using better data or models
Testing changes safely and keeping regulators' expectations in view

questions.text: A retail chain's sales grew this year but its profit stayed flat. Where would you look?
covers: Costs rising faster than sales: stock, staff, rent, delivery
Lower margins from discounts or a shift towards cheaper products
One or two hypotheses, the data that would test them, and a first recommendation

questions.text: Why KPMG, and why this practice?
covers: What the practice does and the kind of clients it serves
Why that work fits your skills and interests
Something specific about KPMG you learnt from its people or work

questions.text: Where do you see yourself in five years, and are you planning a professional qualification?
covers: A realistic goal linked to the practice
Any qualification you're pursuing or considering, and why
How this role helps you get there

tips: Practise reading a short business case and summarising it in a minute: the problem, the key facts, and what you'd recommend.
In a case round, state your structure first, then go area by area, saying your assumptions as you go.
For the technical panel, revise your subject's basics, such as accounting standards, tax or the tools on your CV, and be ready to apply them to an example.
In the group discussion, make two or three structured points, build on others' points rather than talking over them, and offer to summarise at the end.
Keep behavioural answers short: the situation, what you did, and the result, with a number if you can.
Read about one recent change in your field, such as a new accounting rule, a tax change or a technology trend, and what it means for clients.

sources.title: How we recruit: KPMG in India (kpmg.com)

rounds: Online application, with online assessments for many graduate roles
Interview on your experience and motivation, often with behavioural questions
Technical or case discussion for the role
Final interview with a manager, director or partner (for some roles)
